planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, barely covering seed since light aids germination; this taller, old-line strain usually waits until its second year to flower heavily.

directions: Fuji Blue is the classic tall, upright balloon flower strain long grown from seed for cut-flower and border use, producing inflated buds that pop open into wide, star-shaped, violet-blue flowers over a long midsummer season. Plants form an erect clump on a deep taproot that resents transplanting once established, so set out young plants while still small and avoid moving them later. Deadheading extends bloom, and staking is occasionally helpful in windy sites since the stems are taller and less self-supporting than newer dwarf strains. Balloon flower emerges late in spring, so mark the clump's location to avoid digging into the dormant crown while tidying the bed.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost; this compact seed strain often blooms the first year if started early and grown on without interruption.

directions: Sentimental Blue is a dwarf balloon flower strain bred to stay compact and uniformly short, making it well suited to container growing and the front of a border where taller balloon flowers would overwhelm the space. The puffed buds open into violet-blue, star-shaped flowers held well above the tidy foliage mound without need for staking. Give it full sun and well-drained soil, and expect slow emergence in spring from its taproot, which should never be divided or transplanted once settled. Deadhead through summer to keep fresh buds forming.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; this naturally occurring dwarf variety stays shorter and sturdier than the straight species without any staking.

directions: Variety mariesii is a long-cultivated, naturally dwarf and more compact form of the species balloon flower, forming a tight clump of upright stems well under half the height of the typical garden strain. Its inflated balloon-shaped buds open into violet-blue, star-shaped flowers over a long summer season, and the shorter stature means it rarely flops in wind or rain the way taller balloon flowers can. Grow in full sun and average, well-drained soil, and leave the deep taproot undisturbed once planted since the species does not transplant or divide well after establishment. Foliage emerges late in spring, so mark its spot to avoid accidental digging nearby.

planting.note: Plant container-grown or bare-root trees in moist, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun to part shade; this is the true wild species behind the more commonly planted Vossii hybrid. ALL PARTS ARE HIGHLY TOXIC if ingested — keep away from children and pets.

directions: Common laburnum is the parent species behind the showier Laburnum x watereri hybrids, a small deciduous tree with gray-green trifoliate leaves and pendulous chains of fragrant yellow pea-like flowers in late spring. Its flower chains are shorter and somewhat less densely packed than the hybrid's, but the tree is tougher, longer-lived, and sets abundant seed, which self-sows readily where conditions suit it. Plant in full sun to light shade on well-drained, slightly alkaline soil, since it dislikes waterlogged roots, and give it room to develop its naturally rounded, low-branching habit. Every part of the tree, especially the seeds, is poisonous, so site it away from areas where children or grazing animals have access.

planting.note: Plant container-grown or bare-root trees in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Scotch laburnum flowers slightly later than common laburnum and tolerates heavier, less alkaline soils. ALL PARTS ARE HIGHLY TOXIC if ingested — keep away from children and pets.

directions: Scotch laburnum, despite its common name, is native to the mountains of central and southern Europe rather than Scotland, and is one of the two parent species crossed to create the popular Vossii golden chain hybrid. It bears glossy, dark green leaflets and slightly longer, more slender flower chains than common laburnum, opening about two weeks later in late spring to early summer with a lighter, sweeter fragrance. The tree tolerates a wider range of soil pH than common laburnum and holds its glossy foliage cleanly through summer with little disease trouble. As with all laburnums, every part is poisonous if eaten, so keep it away from children and grazing animals.

planting.note: Plant grafted, container-grown trees in lean, very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun; 'Walker' is propagated by grafting its weeping, finely cut growth onto an upright Caragana trunk to form a small standard.

directions: Walker is a weeping, finely textured selection of Siberian pea shrub, grafted atop a short upright trunk so its threadlike, almost ferny foliage cascades to the ground in a small, umbrella-shaped form. Pale yellow pea-like flowers dot the weeping branches in late spring, followed by narrow seed pods, on a plant that tolerates extreme cold, wind, drought, and poor alkaline soils better than almost any other small ornamental tree. Its nitrogen-fixing roots and tough constitution make it a dependable choice for harsh prairie and northern plains gardens where little else weeping survives. Prune only to remove dead wood or crossing growth below the graft union, since the weeping habit needs no shaping to look its best.

planting.note: Plant container-grown or balled-and-burlapped trees in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; 'Vanessa' is the older, longer-established upright Persian ironwood selection, useful as a narrow street or specimen tree.

directions: Vanessa is an upright, vase-shaped Persian ironwood selected decades ago for a narrower, more columnar silhouette than the broadly spreading species, making it useful where a street tree or screen needs height without excessive width. It shares the species' four-season appeal, with small red spring flowers before leaf-out, exfoliating patchwork bark that becomes showier with age, and a long fall color display running through yellow, orange, and red on the same plant at once. Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, and expect the upright habit to loosen slightly and widen somewhat as the tree matures over many years. It adapts to a range of soil types once established and needs little routine pruning beyond removing competing leaders to keep the strongest central framework.

planting.note: WARNING: ALL parts, especially the seeds, are EXTREMELY TOXIC — keep away from children and pets. Start seed indoors 3-4 weeks before the last frost after soaking overnight, and transplant out once the weather is reliably warm.

directions: Carmencita is a compact, fast-growing castor bean selection prized for its dramatic dark bronze-red, deeply lobed foliage topped by bright red, bristly seed clusters held well above the leaves. It stays noticeably shorter and more garden-scaled than old-fashioned tall castor bean strains, making it practical as a dramatic annual accent or temporary screen in a mixed border. Grow in full sun in average to rich, well-drained soil, and water regularly through summer heat for the largest leaves and strongest color. Because every part of the plant is highly toxic if eaten, especially the attractive seeds, site it away from children, pets, and livestock and remove seed heads before they mature if that is a concern.

planting.note: WARNING: ALL parts, especially the seeds, are EXTREMELY TOXIC — keep away from children and pets. Start seed indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost after an overnight soak, and transplant out only once nights stay reliably warm.

directions: New Zealand Purple is a tall, vigorous castor bean strain grown for its nearly black-purple, glossy, star-shaped leaves that darken further with full sun exposure, giving it a more dramatic, moodier color than the bronze-red tones of shorter castor bean selections. Its rapid growth and large stature make it a classic choice for an instant jungle effect or a bold temporary hedge in a single season. Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil and water deeply during dry spells, since the huge leaves transpire heavily in summer heat. Because all parts of the plant, especially the mottled seeds, are highly toxic if ingested, keep it well away from children, pets, and livestock and deadhead seed clusters before they mature if that risk is a concern.
